newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila o/night rate rises despite Central Bank cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila o/night rate rises despite Central Bank cut.

text.p: * Central Bank cuts overnight rate to 14 from 15 pct
The Philippine overnight money inched up to 13.03125 percent from Tuesday's 12.5625 percent as small-lot borrowings pushed the done rates to as high as 15 percent, traders said.
"All the major banks have already squared their position. But small banks were still scrambling for funds in the interbank market," one trader said.
The reduction in the Central Bank's overnight lending rate did not help much, he said. On Wednesday, the Central Bank cut its lending rate to 14 percent from 15 percent.

Most banks were positioning for long-term instruments, especially after the Bureau of Treasury cancelled next Monday's weekly T-bill auction in view of the APEC summit. The auction will be held the following Monday.
"Banks will have so much money in their hands next week without any outlet ... So we are buying bills right now," another trader said.
Secondary rates for government securities softened.
Three-month bills were being bought with effective rates of 11.6 to 11.75 percent, and being sold at 11.7 to 11.875 percent.

Six-month bills were being bid at 12.375 to 12.5 percent and offered at 12.25 to 12.35 percent. One-year bills were being bid at 12.75 to 12.825 percent and offered at 12.6 to 12.715 percent. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
